option_label: Biopsy confirmation of the recurrence, restaging, tumor NGS, and dedicated germline testing

endorsements.designation: Guideline workup mandate (universal germline testing since 2019; tumor NGS for treatment candidates; suspected recurrence confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy)
endorsements.indication_text: All patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma: dedicated germline testing; tumor/somatic NGS for every patient who is a candidate for anti-cancer therapy; suspected recurrence after resection confirmed by imaging and/or biopsy before treatment (March 2026 update).
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 has since posted and could not be read)

endorsements.designation: Guideline recommendation (germline and somatic testing early for all treatment-eligible patients)
endorsements.indication_text: Metastatic pancreatic cancer, all treatment-eligible patients: germline testing plus somatic testing for MSI/dMMR, BRCA, and NTRK alterations, used to select patients for pembrolizumab, olaparib, larotrectinib, or entrectinib.

eligibility_rationale: Nothing in the profile blocks the workup: ECOG 0, and the germline panel and neuropathy grading are blood-and-exam items that need no tissue. The one physical constraint is procedural, the likely vascular invasion around the mass, which shapes the biopsy route rather than whether confirmation is owed.

evidence.effect_size: Recurrence within 12 months of resection carried 20% 1-year post-recurrence survival vs 45% for later recurrence (P<0.001)

toxicity_highlights: Procedural risk of EUS core sampling (bleeding, post-procedure pancreatitis), raised by the likely vascular invasion around the mass

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: This is the same step the experimental ranking carries at rank 1. The staging call opens or closes the daraxonrasib expanded-access protocol, RASolute 303, and the ASP2138 monotherapy arms; the germline draw closes the olaparib gate on both tables; and the neuropathy grade decides taxane exposure on both tracks.

rationale: Everything known about this tumor comes from the December 2025 resection specimen, and the guideline asks for three things before treatment: confirmation of the suspected recurrence by imaging and/or biopsy, tumor NGS for a treatment candidate, and the dedicated germline panel NCCN has mandated in every PDAC patient since 2019, which incidental tumor-NGS reporting does not satisfy. The same workup produces the staging call that decides which standard and which experimental options are open. This is guideline work, not extra caution.
notes: The germline gap is already logged in the biomarker survey (hrd-brca-germline-not-hardened). A CTCAE grade for the residual oxaliplatin neuropathy rides on the same visit as the blood draw and gates several rows below.

endorsements.designation: Recurrence pathway: alternative systemic regimen for recurrence within 6 months of completing adjuvant therapy (gemcitabine-based after fluoropyrimidine-based therapy); clinical trial preferred in this setting
endorsements.indication_text: Recurrence after resection and adjuvant therapy: recurrence within 6 months of completing adjuvant therapy is treated with an alternative regimen not previously used; after fluoropyrimidine-based therapy that means a gemcitabine-based regimen.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

endorsements.designation: III, C as second-line after FOLFIRINOX (Express Update; not EMA- or FDA-approved as second-line therapy). ESMO-MCBS 3 applies to the first-line indication (vs gemcitabine)
endorsements.indication_text: Metastatic pancreatic cancer after first-line FOLFIRINOX: gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel is an option; the graded I, B choice in this position is gemcitabine plus conventional paclitaxel for ECOG PS 0-2.

endorsements.designation: On-label approval (nab-paclitaxel in combination with gemcitabine)
endorsements.indication_text: First-line treatment of patients with metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas, in combination with gemcitabine.

eligibility_rationale: No component repeats what the tumor progressed through, which is the point of the class switch. The gates are in the record: the residual oxaliplatin neuropathy after 10 FOLFIRINOX cycles has no CTCAE grade and nab-paclitaxel adds taxane neurotoxicity on top of it, no organ-function labs exist since the resection, and the recurrence is not yet biopsy-confirmed.
blocking_factors: Residual oxaliplatin neuropathy after 10 FOLFIRINOX cycles is ungraded, and nab-paclitaxel stacks taxane neurotoxicity on the same axis
No post-resection renal, hepatic, or marrow labs on file
The recurrence is radiographic only; the guideline asks for confirmation before treatment

evidence.effect_size: Median OS 8.8 months (95% CI 6.2-9.7); PFS 5.1 months (95% CI 3.2-6.2); ORR 17.5%; grade 3-4 toxicity 40%, neurotoxicity 12.5%
Median OS 8.5 vs 6.7 months, HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.62-0.83), P<0.001; the approval basis, in a different line than this patient's

toxicity_highlights: Grade 3-4 neurotoxicity 12.5% in the AGEO post-FOLFIRINOX cohort, landing on top of ungraded residual oxaliplatin neuropathy
Grade 3-4 toxicity 40% overall in AGEO (neutropenia 12.5%, asthenia 9%, thrombocytopenia 6.5%) with marrow reserve undocumented after 10 chemotherapy cycles

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: RASolute 303 requires consent within 6 weeks of the metastatic diagnosis, so starting this regimen first spends that window, and it changes the line count several CLDN18.2 protocols screen on. In the other direction, its AGEO benchmark (median OS 8.8 months) is the floor the experimental rows are measured against, and it remains available after a trial.

rationale: This is the standard class switch for disease that has progressed through FOLFIRINOX, and the NCCN recurrence pathway routes a recurrence inside 6 months of adjuvant completion, which is this case at about 4 months, to exactly this kind of gemcitabine-based regimen. Expectations should come from the post-FOLFIRINOX data rather than the first-line label: ORR 17.5% and median OS 8.8 months (95% CI 6.2-9.7) in the AGEO cohort. The open items before starting are the neuropathy grade, baseline organ-function labs, and biopsy confirmation of the recurrence.
notes: Two of five board personas ranked this second among all options in the case. The same guideline pathway marks a clinical trial as preferred at this decision point, which is what the experimental table carries.

endorsements.designation: I, B (Express Update)
endorsements.indication_text: After FOLFIRINOX treatment in metastatic pancreatic cancer, gemcitabine plus paclitaxel can be offered to patients with an ECOG PS of 0-2 and a favourable comorbidity profile.

eligibility_rationale: ECOG 0 fits the ESMO wording, but the recommendation was written for metastatic disease after first-line FOLFIRINOX, and this patient's exposure was perioperative with the recurrence still unstaged. The taxane gate is the same as for nab-paclitaxel: the residual oxaliplatin neuropathy has no grade on file.
blocking_factors: Ungraded residual oxaliplatin neuropathy; grade >=3 neuropathy reached 12.3% of the GEMPAX doublet arm
Recurrence not yet biopsy-confirmed or staged

evidence.population: Metastatic PDAC after 5-FU, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan
evidence.effect_size: Median OS 6.4 vs 5.9 months, HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.63-1.20), P=0.41, primary endpoint not met; PFS 3.1 vs 2.0 months, HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.47-0.89); ORR 17.1% vs 4.2%; grade >=3 TRAEs 58.0% vs 27.1%

toxicity_highlights: Grade >=3 neuropathy 12.3% in the doublet arm, the wrong toxicity to add to ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy
Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 58.0% vs 27.1% for gemcitabine alone

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Occupies the same second-line slot as the ranked experimental options, and like any chemotherapy start it spends the RASolute 303 six-week consent window.

rationale: The only randomized grading ESMO gives in this exact position belongs to this doublet: I, B after FOLFIRINOX for ECOG PS 0-2, resting on the GEMPAX trial. The honest reading of GEMPAX is mixed, because the OS primary endpoint was not met (6.4 vs 5.9 months, HR 0.87) while PFS and response improved. NCCN does not carry this specific doublet, and in US practice the gemcitabine-based switch usually means gemcitabine with nab-paclitaxel.

endorsements.designation: On-label approval
endorsements.indication_text: First-line treatment of patients with locally advanced (nonresectable stage II or III) or metastatic (stage IV) adenocarcinoma of the pancreas; indicated for patients previously treated with fluorouracil.

endorsements.designation: III, C (Express Update)
endorsements.indication_text: Metastatic pancreatic cancer after FOLFIRINOX: gemcitabine alone is an option.

endorsements.designation: Recurrence pathway: gemcitabine-based regimen after prior fluoropyrimidine-based therapy
endorsements.indication_text: Recurrence within 6 months of completing adjuvant fluoropyrimidine-based therapy: an alternative, gemcitabine-based regimen.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

eligibility_rationale: The one systemic option on this page that adds no neurotoxic component, so the ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy does not gate it. What is missing is baseline marrow, renal, and hepatic labs, unmeasured since the resection.

evidence.effect_size: Clinical benefit 23.8% vs 4.8%; median OS 5.65 vs 4.41 months (P=0.0025)

evidence.design: randomized phase 3 control arm, second line after FOLFIRINOX
evidence.population: Metastatic PDAC after 5-FU, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan
evidence.effect_size: Median OS 5.9 months (95% CI 4.6-6.9); PFS 2.0 months; ORR 4.2%; the contemporary estimate of what gemcitabine alone does in exactly this position

toxicity_highlights: Myelosuppression and fatigue, with marrow reserve undocumented after 10 chemotherapy cycles
Spares the neuropathy axis entirely, which no taxane-containing row does

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Same second-line slot as the ranked options; starting it spends the RASolute 303 consent window like any other chemotherapy start.

rationale: Single-agent gemcitabine is the fallback inside the same guideline pathway, and its FDA label covers this patient as written, since it is indicated for pancreatic adenocarcinoma previously treated with fluorouracil. It is the least active choice in this position (median OS 5.9 months as the GEMPAX control arm) and the only one that leaves the neuropathy axis alone. In practice the neuropathy grade decides between this row and the taxane doublets.

option_label: Chemoradiation or SBRT to an isolated operative-bed recurrence

endorsements.designation: Recurrence pathway option: chemoradiation or SBRT if not previously given, for local recurrence in the pancreatic operative bed
endorsements.indication_text: Local recurrence in the pancreatic operative bed without metastatic disease: systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation or SBRT (if radiotherapy was not previously given); clinical trial preferred.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

endorsements.designation: Conditional recommendations (2019 clinical practice guideline)
endorsements.indication_text: Locally advanced pancreatic cancer: systemic chemotherapy followed by chemoradiation or SBRT in selected patients; written for intact primaries rather than operative-bed recurrence.

eligibility_rationale: This patient has never been irradiated, so the pathway's 'if not previously given' condition is met. What is not yet established is the load-bearing fact: whether restaging reads this as an isolated local recurrence or as metastatic disease, and whether the vessels involved permit a meaningful dose.
blocking_factors: Restaging has not yet distinguished isolated local recurrence from metastatic disease
Likely vascular invasion constrains dose, fractionation, and technique
toxicity_highlights: GI toxicity of upper-abdominal radiation after a reconstruction, with duodenal or jejunal limb dose as the usual constraint

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The staging call that makes this option live, locally recurrent disease without metastases, is the same call that closes the daraxonrasib expanded-access protocol, RASolute 303, and the ASP2138 monotherapy arms, while ASP5834 accepts locally advanced unresectable disease. Recent radiotherapy is itself an exclusion window in several protocols, so the timing question runs in both directions.

rationale: If restaging reads this as an isolated operative-bed recurrence, radiotherapy is the standard local option, usually alongside or after systemic therapy, and this patient's lack of prior radiation keeps the pathway's condition met. The supporting evidence is institutional series rather than randomized data, and the likely vascular invasion constrains what dose is achievable. Re-resection of an isolated local recurrence is reported from high-volume centers but is not carried by NCCN or ESMO as a standard option, so it is not listed as one here.
notes: The workup row at the top of the table is what closes this gate; the same restaging read controls the metastatic-only experimental routes.

endorsements.designation: On-label approval (2019)
endorsements.indication_text: Maintenance treatment of adults with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma whose disease has not progressed on at least 16 weeks of a first-line platinum-based chemotherapy regimen; BRACAnalysis CDx is the companion diagnostic.

endorsements.designation: Guideline recommendation
endorsements.indication_text: Olaparib maintenance for patients with germline BRCA mutation and metastatic pancreatic cancer without progression after at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum-based chemotherapy.

endorsements.designation: Maintenance option, germline BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic disease after platinum response
endorsements.indication_text: Germline BRCA1/2-mutated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma without progression on first-line platinum-based therapy.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

eligibility_rationale: Both gates are open: germline status is unknown because the dedicated panel has never been drawn (incidental tumor-NGS reporting does not rule these genes out), and the label's platinum criterion is unmet as written, since the recurrence came about 4 months after platinum-containing adjuvant therapy rather than after 16 or more weeks of first-line platinum without progression.
blocking_factors: Germline BRCA1/2 status unknown; dedicated multigene panel never drawn
Label requires no progression on >=16 weeks of first-line platinum, which this course does not satisfy as written
Recurrence 4 months after platinum-containing adjuvant therapy argues against the platinum sensitivity the strategy assumes

biomarker_requirement.biomarker: Germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant (PALB2 by extension, off-label)
biomarker_requirement.threshold: Deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1/2 variant by BRACAnalysis CDx or equivalent dedicated germline panel

evidence.population: Germline BRCA-mutated metastatic PDAC without progression on >=16 weeks first-line platinum

evidence.effect_size: Median OS 19.0 vs 19.2 months, HR 0.83, P=0.3487; no survival gain

toxicity_highlights: Grade >=3 AEs 40% vs 23% on placebo (anemia, fatigue, nausea), 5% discontinuation

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Same strategy as rank 5 of the experimental ranking; it sits in both tables because it is FDA-approved and biomarker-gated. The blood draw that closes its gate is part of the workup bundle at the top of both tables.

rationale: The one biomarker-gated FDA label in this disease, kept visible chiefly to keep the germline panel from slipping. Pre-test probability is roughly 5-7% for germline BRCA1/2 in unselected PDAC, and even in a carrier the demonstrated benefit is progression-free time (HR 0.53) with final OS flat at 19.0 vs 19.2 months. The label as written also presumes a platinum response this course has not shown, so any use here would be argued case by case after a positive panel.
notes: A PALB2 or somatic-only BRCA finding would not satisfy the germline-defined label and would need a prior-authorization argument; the recurrence NGS carries the somatic half of that question at no extra cost.

option_label: Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy and nutritional support

endorsements.designation: Supportive-care recommendation
endorsements.indication_text: Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency after pancreatectomy or from pancreatic cancer: pancreatic enzyme replacement with nutritional assessment and support.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

endorsements.designation: AGA Clinical Practice Update, Best Practice Advice (2023)
endorsements.indication_text: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, with pancreatic resection among the high-risk settings: diagnose, treat with pancreatic enzyme replacement, and monitor nutrition including fat-soluble vitamins and bone health.

endorsements.designation: On-label approval (pancrelipase products)
endorsements.indication_text: Treatment of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, including insufficiency due to pancreatectomy.

eligibility_rationale: The record describes the resection as a Whipple (per the user; the operative report was not supplied), which makes exocrine insufficiency probable, but no fecal elastase, weight trend, or symptom record is on file to say whether replacement is already in place or adequate.
toxicity_highlights: Minimal at standard dosing; the practical failure mode is underdosing, not toxicity

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Runs alongside any systemic, radiotherapy, or trial route and conflicts with none of them. Nutritional state feeds the screening labs and performance-status criteria every protocol on the experimental table applies.

rationale: After a pancreatic resection, and with a new mass in the remnant, exocrine insufficiency is the default assumption until tested, and untreated insufficiency quietly erodes the weight, albumin, and performance status every treatment plan on this page depends on. Enzyme replacement is inexpensive, on-label, and carried by both NCCN and the AGA. Glycemic surveillance for post-pancreatectomy diabetes belongs in the same visit.

option_label: Early palliative care and a goals-of-care discussion

endorsements.designation: Guideline recommendation (2024 update)
endorsements.indication_text: Patients with advanced cancer: dedicated palliative care services early in the disease course, concurrent with active treatment.

endorsements.designation: Supportive-care principles (pancreatic guideline)
endorsements.indication_text: Advanced or recurrent pancreatic cancer: symptom management and palliative care integrated with disease-directed treatment.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

eligibility_rationale: No profile fact bears on eligibility; the recommendation applies to every patient in this disease state, at any performance status.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Explicitly concurrent: choosing aggressive treatment, a trial, or neither does not change the recommendation. Documenting goals of care would also firm up the efficacy/toxicity weighting the rest of the case currently carries as an assumed default.

rationale: A recurrence 4 months after completing adjuvant therapy for pancreatic cancer is the situation the early palliative care evidence was built for, and ASCO's recommendation is concurrent with treatment, not instead of it. The preferences on file weight efficacy at 0.7 as an assumed default, and the intake itself flags that goals of care are undocumented; a goals-of-care conversation is how that number stops being an assumption. This row competes with nothing on either table.

endorsements.designation: On-label approval (2015)
endorsements.indication_text: Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas after disease progression following gemcitabine-based therapy, in combination with fluorouracil and leucovorin.

endorsements.designation: Subsequent-therapy option after gemcitabine-based therapy
endorsements.indication_text: Advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma previously treated with gemcitabine-based therapy.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

eligibility_rationale: Not an option today: the label and the guideline slot both sit after gemcitabine-based therapy, which this patient has not yet received. It becomes the on-label next step if a gemcitabine-based second line is used and fails.
blocking_factors: Label requires prior progression on gemcitabine-based therapy, which has not yet been given
Ten prior irinotecan-containing cycles with recurrence at 4 months raise a topoisomerase-1 cross-resistance question the NAPOLI-1 population does not answer

evidence.effect_size: Median OS 6.1 vs 4.2 months for 5-FU/LV alone, HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.49-0.92), P=0.012

toxicity_highlights: Grade 3-4 neutropenia 27%, diarrhea 13%, fatigue 14% in the combination arm

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: IBI343 carries an exatecan payload, another topoisomerase-1 poison. In either order, the second topoisomerase-1 exposure faces possible cross-resistance, and no published data settle that sequence.

rationale: Carried for the decision after this one: if a gemcitabine-based second line is used and fails, this becomes the on-label subsequent therapy. The caveat the label does not carry is that this tumor has already seen 10 irinotecan-containing cycles, and how much activity a liposomal formulation recovers after that has no direct answer in the NAPOLI-1 population, which was largely irinotecan-naive.

option_label: Biliary decompression and GI symptom management, if obstruction develops

endorsements.designation: Principles of palliation and supportive care
endorsements.indication_text: Biliary or gastric outlet obstruction from pancreatic cancer: endoscopic decompression preferred where feasible, with percutaneous and surgical routes for selected cases.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

eligibility_rationale: The profile has no bilirubin, no cholangitis history, and no operative report, so neither the biliary anatomy after the December 2025 reconstruction nor any sign of current obstruction is on file. The missing facts are a baseline hepatic panel and the operative anatomy.
toxicity_highlights: Procedure-related cholangitis and stent occlusion over time; altered post-surgical anatomy can force a percutaneous or EUS-guided route
rationale: A recurrence in the pancreatic remnant can obstruct the biliary limb or the GI tract as it grows, and the standard response is endoscopic decompression rather than anything on the treatment tables. Nothing in the record says obstruction exists today, so this is carried for the moment it appears: the first bilirubin rise or gastric-outlet symptom. It is worth anticipating because post-surgical anatomy can make endoscopic access slower to arrange.

endorsements.designation: Preferred regimen, first-line metastatic or locally advanced disease, good performance status (FOLFIRINOX or mFOLFIRINOX)
endorsements.indication_text: Treatment-naive metastatic or locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma with good performance status; the recurrence pathway routes recurrence within 6 months of adjuvant completion to an alternative regimen instead.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

endorsements.designation: I, A first line; ESMO-MCBS 5 (vs gemcitabine)
endorsements.indication_text: Treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic cancer, fit patients.

eligibility_rationale: Ten total cycles across the neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings, with recurrence about 4 months after completion.
prior_exposure_note: mFOLFIRINOX x6 neoadjuvant in 2025 with a partial response, then R0 resection in December 2025 (0/34 nodes, CAP tumor regression grade 2), then adjuvant FOLFIRINOX x4 completed per plan in March 2026. Treatment stopped at planned completion, not for toxicity or progression. A new pancreatic body mass appeared in July 2026, about 4 months later, which the NCCN recurrence pathway treats as progression through the regimen for sequencing purposes. Residual oxaliplatin neuropathy persists and has not been graded.

evidence.effect_size: Median OS 11.1 vs 6.8 months vs gemcitabine, HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.45-0.73), P<0.001
Median DFS 21.6 vs 12.8 months vs gemcitabine, HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.46-0.73), P<0.001

toxicity_highlights: Oxaliplatin re-exposure into an already injured peripheral nervous system
rationale: Carried so the record is explicit about why the strongest first-line regimen in this disease is not being re-offered: the patient has had 10 total cycles across the neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings, and recurrence 4 months after completion reads as functional resistance under the guideline's 6-month convention. Re-challenge in this window has no guideline carriage and would re-expose an already injured peripheral nervous system to oxaliplatin.

endorsements.designation: On-label approval (2024)
endorsements.indication_text: First-line treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma: liposomal irinotecan in combination with oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin.

endorsements.designation: Preferred regimen, first-line metastatic disease, good performance status
endorsements.indication_text: Treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with good performance status; the same guideline's recurrence pathway routes recurrence within 6 months of adjuvant completion to an alternative regimen.
endorsements.version_or_date: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 (verified 22 April 2026; v3.2026 posted, not read)

endorsements.designation: Preferred first-line option for fit patients (Express Update); ESMO-MCBS 2 (vs gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel)
endorsements.indication_text: Treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic cancer, fit patients.

eligibility_rationale: The regimen re-runs fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan within months of the tumor progressing through 10 cycles of the same three drug classes, and the ungraded oxaliplatin neuropathy independently gates a platinum re-exposure.
blocking_factors: Recurrence about 4 months after completing 10 cycles of 5-FU/oxaliplatin/irinotecan-based therapy; NCCN routes this to an alternative regimen
Ungraded residual oxaliplatin neuropathy gates oxaliplatin re-exposure
NAPOLI 3, the approval basis, enrolled treatment-naive metastatic patients

evidence.effect_size: Median OS 11.1 vs 9.2 months vs gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.70-0.99), P=0.036

toxicity_highlights: Grade >=3 TEAEs 87% in NAPOLI 3, including the oxaliplatin neurotoxicity this patient already carries a residue of
rationale: On paper the 2024 label covers first-line metastatic disease, and a patient entering her first metastatic line could be read into it. In practice this regimen re-runs fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, and irinotecan within months of the tumor progressing through 10 cycles of the same three classes, and the NCCN recurrence pathway routes a recurrence inside 6 months of adjuvant completion away from exactly that. Set aside for re-exposure and neuropathy reasons, not for lack of an approval.
